title: The Iḍāfa Possessive Structure
lede: Build two- and multi-noun iḍāfa chains, control definiteness, case, tāʾ marbūṭa and adjective placement.

items.feedback: First noun has no article/tanwīn; second is genitive.
Final indefinite noun makes chain indefinite.

items.prompt: What happens to dual/plural nūn in idāfa?

items.feedback: Suffix can be final definite term.

items.prompt: Which adjective describes door in بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ الْجَدِيدُ?
Adjective for “new door of the school”.

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا هَذَا مُهِمٌّ؟
Build two- and multi-noun iḍāfa chains, control definiteness, case, tāʾ marbūṭa and adjective placement.
Recognise and build the core form.
Use the form accurately in sentence roles and agreement.
Explain case, exceptions and interaction with iḍāfa.
Answer first; then use the explanations to repair uncertainty.
Iḍāfa joins nouns into one possessive or associative unit. English often uses “of” or apostrophe-s; Arabic uses order and grammatical marking.
- takes case from its sentence role
[callout] Definiteness travels from the final term: بَابُ مَدْرَسَةٍ = a school door; بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ = the school door; بَابُ مَدْرَسَتِي = my school’s door.

TABLE: Meaning | Arabic | Notice // the school headteacher’s office | مَكْتَبُ مُدِيرِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ | Only final term takes article // the two class teachers | مُعَلِّمَا الصَّفِّ | dual nūn drops // the school teachers | مُعَلِّمُو الْمَدْرَسَةِ | sound plural nūn drops // the student’s bag | حَقِيبَةُ الطَّالِبِ | ة pronounced t in connection

[callout/warning] Do not insert an adjective blindly. Place it after the completed chain and make its gender reveal the noun it modifies: بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ الْجَدِيدُ (new door) versus بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ الْجَدِيدَةِ (new school).
Use the noun system to extract and communicate real information.
فِي مَدْرَسَتِنَا طَالِبَانِ جَدِيدَانِ وَمُعَلِّمَاتٌ خَبِيرَاتٌ. الْفُصُولُ وَاسِعَةٌ، وَمَكْتَبُ مُدِيرِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمَدْخَلِ.
Underline every noun relevant to this lesson and explain its form.
Choose five nouns. Say the singular, dual and/or plural form required by this lesson, then use each in a complete sentence.
Write 8–12 connected sentences about your school, home or local area. Use at least six target noun forms from this lesson and underline them.
[callout] Model: فِي حَيِّي مَدْرَسَتَانِ كَبِيرَتَانِ، وَمَكْتَبَةُ الْحَيِّ مُفِيدَةٌ لِلطُّلَّابِ.
Plan visually, label your examples in Arabic, then check each target form.
Complete the same task on paper. Underline the target noun forms and annotate the rule used.
Apply the rules without relying on the explanation panels.
